evidence.claim: ECM advisers now put Anthropic IPO value near $1T, down from $1.2-1.45T pre-selloff; the article cites $895.4B of non-cancellable infrastructure commitments with take-or-pay true-ups (single source).
evidence.numbers: The $895.4B is well above the $542-567B read from the S-1 in October and is not reconciled; a lower valuation means the largest tenant raises less equity against fixed commitments.

evidence.claim: Microsoft is trimming its neocloud supplier list (single source).
evidence.numbers: Fewer large buyers per neocloud raises concentration on the labs that remain.

evidence.claim: Anthropic lease is about $19bn of about $27bn contracted revenue, and needs Google support because Anthropic is not investment-grade.
evidence.numbers: About 70% of contracted revenue from one lab (derived).

evidence.claim: Riot's Corsicana lease puts 1,101 of 1,151 contracted MW with one lab, named Anthropic PBC in the 10-Q; on the call no analyst asked about credit or termination.
evidence.numbers: 910 MW, about $28bn over 15 years; about 96% of MW; take-or-pay regardless of utilization.

evidence.claim: Jassy called the $578bn backlog 'well-diversified' and listed new AWS deals with Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI and others.
evidence.numbers: No customer split was given. Amazon's Anthropic holdings rose to $238.7bn ($92.5bn preferred plus $146.2bn notes at fair value, +$48.3bn QoQ) and it completed the $50bn OpenAI investment ($21.3bn in 3Q); words and numbers diverge.

evidence.claim: Cloud backlog reached $560.8bn (+$46.9bn QoQ), including $16.8bn with Crux AI, a related-party joint venture. On the call Google named Anthropic (direct and via Broadcom), Apple, and new lab customers as TPU buyers; about 100 customers use TPUs.
evidence.numbers: Management says most backlog is 'typical GCP contracts' but gives no customer split; TPU revenue is not sized.

evidence.claim: Microsoft recorded $10.0bn of revenue from OpenAI in 1Q FY27, including revenue-share payments; the OpenAI receivable rose to $7.2bn from $6.0bn. Management did not give RPO growth excluding OpenAI and deflected a question on model mix.
evidence.numbers: OpenAI was 10.8% of 1Q revenue vs 7.3% of FY26 revenue, while commercial RPO was flat QoQ at $677bn and bookings fell 12% (single source). Fortune separately reports Anthropic committed at least $44.9bn of Microsoft compute through May 2033 (single source).

evidence.claim: Anthropic's S-1 shows $265.6B of future fixed or minimum compute purchases and $321.4B of leases not yet commenced as of June 2026, separate long-dated buckets, some conditional. First-half 2026 revenue was $16.3B with compute expense at 55% of sales, down from 201% a year earlier. One lab's committed book now exceeds the entire landlord bond market many times over.
evidence.numbers: $265.6B purchases + $321.4B leases vs $16.3B H1 revenue; compute 55% of sales
evidence.source: Anthropic S-1 as summarized by Sridhar Ramaswamy, 27 Oct 2026 (figures not yet checked against the filing)

evidence.claim: S-1 discloses Anthropic Direct: third parties secure land and power and operate dedicated sites, Anthropic leases them; $125.2B of five-year lease payments excluding interest.
evidence.numbers: Total commitments $542-567B against $11.6B of Q2 revenue; compute cost $5.6B in that quarter. MW and counterparties undisclosed.

evidence.claim: Commitment rose to up to $120.5B through 2029 with about $3.1B a month at full delivery. (exit terms single source)
evidence.numbers: Non-cancelable periods reportedly end January and March 2027, then 90-day exits either way, so the headline overstates firm revenue.

evidence.claim: SpaceX's compute business rests on two tenants: Anthropic (all of Colossus 1, $1.25B a month through May 2029, up to $84.5B per Anthropic's prospectus) and Google ($920M a month to June 2029, called 'bridge capacity'). Most agreements can be ended on 90 days' notice.
evidence.numbers: Contracted cloud revenue $14.1B at Q2 plus $6.7B of six-month deals; the two named tenants are about $26B a year.
evidence.source: SpaceX S-1 and Q2 call; TechRepublic on Google terms; Anthropic prospectus via BigGo

evidence.claim: Nscale's S-1 shows Microsoft and Anthropic at about 85% of contracted backlog, anchored by a $44.6B six-year Anthropic deal in West Virginia; its largest customer was 52% of H1 revenue.
evidence.numbers: Microsoft has now walked from one site.

evidence.claim: Anthropic is reported offering Blackstone above 10% on $9B of debt backed by its five-year chip lease payments.
evidence.numbers: Lab is now borrowing directly against its compute leases (single source).
evidence.source: The Star, citing Reuters and the FT

evidence.claim: Q3 revenue of $16.8B, up 45% on the quarter after 145% in Q2, from an investor presentation (unaudited).
Reporting clarified annualized revenue closer to $50B than the $68B circulating.
Draft prospectus shows at least $518B of compute commitments over a decade, about 80% non-cancellable.
Nearly all contracted growth traces to Anthropic, directly or through Fluidstack.

question: How exposed is the buildout to two labs?
summary: Exposure keeps rising while the labs' own funding gets less certain. Anthropic's S-1 showed $542-567B of compute commitments and Anthropic Direct leases; an ECM report now cites $895.4B of non-cancellable commitments (single source, unreconciled) as its IPO valuation slips toward $1T from $1.2-1.45T. Microsoft trimming neocloud suppliers (single source) leaves the labs a larger share of remaining demand. The SpaceX deal's reported 90-day exits from 2027 (single source) show those commitments are less firm than headlines. Status stays strengthening.
title: Concentration on Anthropic and OpenAI
